name: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning (Responder)
description: Poison LLMNR and NBT-NS broadcast name resolution to capture NTLMv2 hashes from domain hosts. No credentials required.

recommended.note: Crack captured NTLMv2 hash with hashcat

notes: Best during business hours. Disable SMB/HTTP in Responder.conf if only capturing, not responding.

defense.why_it_works: When Windows fails DNS resolution, it falls back to LLMNR (UDP 5355) and NBT-NS (UDP 137) multicast queries on the local subnet. Any host on the same broadcast domain can respond with a spoofed IP. Windows then connects to that IP via SMB or HTTP, sending NTLMv2 challenge-response hashes. Responder automates spoofed responses and captures/relays these hashes.
defense.prerequisites: Attacker on same L2 broadcast domain as victim. LLMNR or NBT-NS not disabled by GPO. Responder or Inveigh running. For relay: SMB signing disabled on target hosts (default on workstations).
defense.impact: T1557.001 Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay. Captures Net-NTLMv2 hashes for offline cracking, or relays to authenticate to other hosts without cracking.
defense.detection:
LLMNR/NBT-NS queries followed by responses from unexpected IPs. IDS/NDR: unexpected LLMNR response from non-DC. Sysmon Event 3: SMB connection to unexpected IP after name resolution failure. Event 4624 on relay target sourced from attacker IP. MDI: NTLM relay detection. Zeek: LLMNR response from non-authoritative source.
Detect suspicious DNS/ARP poisoning attempts, unauthorized modifications to registry/network configuration, or abnormal TLS downgrade activity; correlate with subsequent unusual network flows or authentication events (DET0296/AN0823). Unauthorized edits to /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf, or suspicious ARP broadcasts correlated with unexpected network sessions (AN0824). Unauthorized edits to system configuration profiles, unexpected certificate trust changes, or abnormal ARP/DNS interception patterns (AN0825). Unauthorized firmware/configuration changes enabling AiTM positioning: route injection, DNS spoofing, SSL downgrade; sudden changes to routing tables or image file integrity failures (AN0826).
defense.artifacts: IDS alert: LLMNR response from non-DC | Event 4624 on relay target with source = attacker IP | Zeek llmnr.log: unexpected responder | Responder.db on attacker (captured hashes) | SMB connection to attacker IP in netflow
defense.prevention:
Disable LLMNR via GPO: Computer Config → Admin Templates → Network → DNS Client → Turn off multicast name resolution: Enabled. Disable NBT-NS via NIC settings or GPO. Require SMB signing on all hosts to prevent relay. Deploy MDI.
Disable or Remove Feature or Program: Disable legacy network protocols that may be used to intercept traffic if not needed.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Ensure all wired/wireless traffic is encrypted; use Kerberos; protect web traffic containing credentials with SSL/TLS.
Filter Network Traffic: Use network appliances and host-based security to block unnecessary traffic, including legacy protocols leveraged for AiTM.
Limit Access to Resource Over Network: Limit access to network infrastructure that can reshape traffic or produce AiTM conditions.
Network Intrusion Prevention: Use IDS/IPS to identify AiTM traffic patterns.
Network Segmentation: Isolate infrastructure components that do not require broad network access.
User Training: Train users to be suspicious about certificate errors; adversaries may use their own certs to intercept HTTPS.
defense.evasion: Use Responder --analyze first to observe without poisoning. HTTPS relay for environments with SMB signing. Run during high-activity hours when DNS failures are frequent.
defense.misconfiguration: LLMNR enabled (default on all Windows). NBT-NS enabled. SMB signing not required on workstations (default). No IDS rule for unexpected LLMNR responses.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# LLMNR enabled (Windows default):
# GPO: Computer Config → Admin Templates → Network → DNS Client
# → Turn off multicast name resolution: NOT CONFIGURED

# SMB signing not required on workstations:
Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select-Object RequireSecuritySignature  # False = relay possible

# NBT-NS enabled (default Windows NIC binding)
defense.secure_config:
# Disable LLMNR via GPO:
# Computer Config → Admin Templates → Network → DNS Client
# → Turn off multicast name resolution: Enabled

# Disable NBT-NS:
$adapters = Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration -Filter 'IPEnabled=True'
foreach ($a in $adapters) { $a.SetTcpipNetbios(2) }  # 2 = Disable

# Require SMB signing everywhere:
Set-SmbClientConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true -Force
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true -Force

# GPO equivalent:
# Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Local Policies → Security Options
# → Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always): Enabled
# → Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always): Enabled
